questions.topic: Craft and Structure · Words in Context
questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from the 1895 poem “The Song My Paddle Sings” by Emily Pauline Johnson

(Tekahionwake).

West wind blow from your prairie nest,

Blow from the mountains, blow from the west.

The sail is idle, the sailor too;

O! wind of the west, we wait for you.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, what does the word “idle” most nearly mean?
questions.options_raw:
A. Lựa chọn A
B. Lựa chọn B
C. Lựa chọn C
D. Lựa chọn D

questions.pooe_breakdown:
• Đáp án ĐÚNG: B. Inactive - Phản ánh chính xác ngữ cảnh học thuật và sắc thái ý nghĩa của câu.
• Loại A. Untrustworthy - Sai sắc thái hoặc không ăn nhập với đối tượng được miêu tả.
• Loại C. Unsupported - Sai sắc thái hoặc không ăn nhập với đối tượng được miêu tả.
• Loại D. Nonsensical - Sai sắc thái hoặc không ăn nhập với đối tượng được miêu tả.

option_explanations.A: Loại A - A (Untrustworthy) - Không phù hợp ngữ cảnh bài thi. Từ này mang nét nghĩa lệch hướng, sai sắc thái biểu cảm hoặc không tạo thành cụm từ kết hợp tự nhiên (collocation) với các thành phần trong câu.
option_explanations.B: ĐÁP ÁN ĐÚNG. B (Inactive) - Mang nét nghĩa hoàn toàn khớp với ngữ cảnh bài đọc. Từ này diễn đạt chuẩn xác bản chất đối tượng và liên kết chặt chẽ với các chi tiết xung quanh.
option_explanations.C: Loại C - C (Unsupported) - Không phù hợp ngữ cảnh bài thi. Từ này mang nét nghĩa lệch hướng, sai sắc thái biểu cảm hoặc không tạo thành cụm từ kết hợp tự nhiên (collocation) với các thành phần trong câu.
option_explanations.D: Loại D - D (Nonsensical) - Không phù hợp ngữ cảnh bài thi. Từ này mang nét nghĩa lệch hướng, sai sắc thái biểu cảm hoặc không tạo thành cụm từ kết hợp tự nhiên (collocation) với các thành phần trong câu.

carbon dioxide levels that occurred at the time.

questions.passage:
Information from the Great Sunflower Project helps scientists address pollinator population-size declines

caused by habitat loss. Participants monitor which pollinators visit specific plants and the frequency of

those visits. Scientists then use this information to determine which plant species best support pollinators

and identify where those plant species have declined. Without bees, butterflies, and other pollinators

performing their vital role in plant reproduction and food production, ecosystems would suffer—making

the conservation efforts informed by this citizen science project all the more important!

mesophotic conditions. In 2018, Luiz Rocha and colleagues studied stony corals in the two zones in

Caribbean and Indo-Pacific waters. Based on the depths at which those corals are now found, the species

questions.topic: Information and Ideas · Inferences
questions.passage:
The roseate spoonbill and the glossy ibis are long-legged birds that live in wetlands, like the Everglades in

Florida. Laura D’Acunto and colleagues wanted to know how these birds choose an area in which to live.

They looked at features of these birds’ habitats, such as how quickly water drains from the area and the

amount of tree-canopy cover there is in the area. They found that roseate spoonbills prefer areas with

extensive canopy cover, but this was not true for glossy ibises. The researchers therefore concluded that

wetland-management strategies that increase the amount of tree canopy in potential wetland bird habitats

are less likely to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.options_raw:
A. Lựa chọn A
B. Lựa chọn B
C. Lựa chọn C
D. Lựa chọn D

questions.tier2_hint: Tóm tắt các tiền đề: Nếu A dẫn đến B, và B gặp điều kiện C, thì kết quả tất yếu phải là gì? Chú ý các từ hạn định (qualifiers) như 'may', 'likely', 'some' để tránh bẫy cực đoan.

questions.topic: Expression of Ideas · Rhetorical Synthesis
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

•  From the 1930s to the 1960s, movie theaters in Black communities often created new versions of

posters for films to promote Black actors and themes relevant to Black audiences.

•  The original studio poster for Imitation of Life (1934) did not credit any of the film’s Black actors.

•  A poster at a Black-owned theater in Harlem, New York, gave top billing to the film’s Black star, Louise

Beavers, and highlighted the film’s theme of Black American identity.

•  According to media historian Ellen Scott, such revisions “centralized African American narrative

presence and subjectivity.”
questions.prompt:
The student wants to compare the studio poster for Imitation of Life to the Harlem theater poster. Which
choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

Popularized in sixteenth- and seventeenth-century England by such poets as William Shakespeare and Mary

Wroth, the sonnet sequence (a series of fourteen-line poems unified by overarching thematic concerns)

remains a prevalent poetic genre. Although the sonnet’s intricate, rule-bound structure makes writing even

one sonnet—let alone an entire series—intrinsically challenging, more recent poets from Gwendolyn

Brooks to Brandy Nālani McDougall have undertaken sonnet sequences, likely in part because of the

opportunity the genre presents for showcasing a poet’s virtuosity and ingenuity.

questions.topic: Information and Ideas · Central Ideas and Details
questions.passage:
Text 1

In 2012 Jeonju, South Korea, was named a City of Gastronomy by UNESCO in recognition of the city’s

unique food culture. The honor is well known among both residents of the city and tourists who visit.

Simply by selecting Jeonju, UNESCO has helped bring awareness to local recipes, cooking practices, and

chefs and has provided a significant boost to the city’s tourism industry.

Text 2

Many people in Jeonju’s restaurant industry hoped that food tourism would increase after the city was

chosen as a City of Gastronomy in 2012. However, as researcher Eerang Park and colleagues argue, cities

must still create effective marketing strategies to benefit fully from being named a City of Gastronomy.

Without the intentional effort that was made to promote the city’s food scene, many current and potential

visitors to Jeonju would not even be aware that it’s home to uniquely delicious food.
questions.prompt:
Which choice best describes a difference in how the authors of the texts view the benefits of being named
a City of Gastronomy?
questions.options_raw:
A. Lựa chọn A
B. Lựa chọn B
C. Lựa chọn C
D. Lựa chọn D

questions.passage:
Like all species of baleen whales, the humpback whale feeds on tiny creatures known as krill by filtering

water through bristlelike keratin structures called baleen plates. In this way, baleen whales can eat up to 30

percent of their total mass per day. And while no one would call the humpback whale small—it can have a

mass as high as 30,000 kg—it is one of the smaller baleen whales and is much smaller than the fin whale,

which can weigh a whopping 80,000 kg and consume as much as 24,000 kg of krill per day.

fin whales?

The following text is from Nathaniel Hawthorne’s 1830 short story “Sir William Phips.”

The knowledge, communicated by the historian and biographer, is analogous to that which we acquire of a

country by the map,—minute, perhaps, and accurate, and available for all necessary purposes, but cold and

naked, and wholly destitute of the mimic charm produced by landscape painting. These defects are partly

remediable, and even without an absolute violation of literal truth, although by methods rightfully

interdicted to professors of biographical exactness.

questions.passage:
Enacted in societies as disparate as early modern Florence and Ming China, sumptuary laws—restrictions

on personal spending on luxury—often focused on matters of dress, such as the patterns and motifs

allowed for different social classes. In the early modern European context, such laws were meant to keep

appearance consistent with class status. However, creativity posed an ongoing challenge: new modes of

dress not covered by the laws would emerge and be adopted across social classes. Despite frequent

revision, sumptuary laws struggled to keep pace with the flourishing European fashion industry.

questions.topic: Expression of Ideas · Rhetorical Synthesis

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

•  Joeun Kim Aatchim is a Korean-born, New York–based visual artist.

•  She has a condition known as stereo blindness, which means her eyes don’t fully sync to form an

image.

•  Rather than drawing subjects while looking at them, she relies on an accumulation of visual memory.

•  Her drawings feature transparent, overlapping images of their subjects and thus have a hazy

appearance.

•  Transparency (2019) features a woman shown from several perspectives.

•  Two Mini Lilies (2019) features a pair of lilies in separate glass vases.

The student wants to describe Aatchim’s artistic process. Which choice most effectively uses relevant
information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
